answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 49% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the tide registry records each claim and the yarrow audit publishes every slash. A farm must therefore either lie, which the grove graph proves on replay, or recruit 85 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 38 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
